instructions:
Set up your Neovim config in Lua: ~/.config/nvim/init.lua.

1. If you already have ~/.config/nvim/init.vim, back it up first:
     cp ~/.config/nvim/init.vim ~/.config/nvim/init.vim.bak
   No init.vim? Skip to step 2.
2. Create ~/.config/nvim/init.lua. If you had an init.vim, translate each `set` line to Lua:
     set number          ->  vim.opt.number = true
     set tabstop=4       ->  vim.opt.tabstop = 4
     set mouse=a         ->  vim.opt.mouse = 'a'
     set clipboard=unnamedplus -> vim.opt.clipboard = 'unnamedplus'
     set cc=80           ->  vim.opt.colorcolumn = '80'
   `syntax on` and `filetype plugin indent on` are Neovim defaults, so you can drop them.
   `set nocompatible` and `set ttyfast` do nothing in Neovim, so drop them too.
   Starting fresh? A small baseline (change the values to taste):
     vim.opt.number = true
     vim.opt.expandtab = true
     vim.opt.shiftwidth = 4
     vim.opt.tabstop = 4
     vim.opt.ignorecase = true
3. If you used plugins in init.vim (e.g. with vim-plug), leave them out for now:
   lesson 10.4 sets up a Lua plugin manager.
4. If you had an init.vim, move it away so the two configs don't conflict:
     mv ~/.config/nvim/init.vim ~/.config/nvim/init.vim.old   (you already have the .bak)
5. Restart nvim and check your options, e.g. :set number? tabstop? expandtab?

Tip: write init.lua *in nvim*. Use your week 1-9 skills, e.g. paste the old lines
and convert them with :s and macros. :help lua-guide-options is the reference.

# --- shared helpers (read-only checks) ---
fail=0
ok()  { printf '  \033[32m✔\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; }
bad() { printf '  \033[31m✘\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; [ -n "$2" ] && printf '      → %s\n' "$2"; fail=1; }
# q 'lua expression' : evaluate with your real config, print the result
q() { nvim --headless -c "lua io.stdout:write(tostring($1))" -c 'qa!' 2>/dev/null; }
CFG=$(nvim --headless --clean -c 'lua io.stdout:write(vim.fn.stdpath("config"))' -c 'qa!' 2>/dev/null)
DATA=$(nvim --headless --clean -c 'lua io.stdout:write(vim.fn.stdpath("data"))' -c 'qa!' 2>/dev/null)
startup_errors() { nvim --headless -c 'qa!' 2>&1 | grep -iE 'error|E[0-9]{3,4}:' | head -5; }
finish() { if [ $fail -eq 0 ]; then echo "All checks passed."; exit 0; else echo "Not done yet - fix the ✘ items and run: vimdrill --check"; exit 1; fi; }
# ---

echo "Checking your Lua config in $CFG"
[ -f "$CFG/init.lua" ] && ok "init.lua exists" || bad "no $CFG/init.lua" "create it (step 2)"
[ ! -f "$CFG/init.vim" ] && ok "init.vim is gone (no conflict)" || bad "init.vim still exists" "move it away (step 4)"
if [ -f "$CFG/init.lua" ]; then
  e=$(startup_errors); [ -z "$e" ] && ok "nvim starts without errors" || bad "startup errors: $e" "run nvim and read :messages"
  grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*vim\.(opt|o)\.[a-z]+' "$CFG/init.lua" && ok "init.lua sets options in Lua" || bad "no vim.opt / vim.o lines in init.lua" "step 2"
fi
finish

instructions:
Give yourself a leader key and your first mappings, in init.lua.

1. At the very TOP of init.lua (before any mapping):
     vim.g.mapleader = ' '
     vim.g.maplocalleader = ' '
2. Add these mappings (vim.keymap.set(mode, lhs, rhs, opts)):
     vim.keymap.set('n', '<leader>w', '<cmd>write<CR>', { desc = 'Save file' })
     vim.keymap.set('n', '<leader>q', '<cmd>quit<CR>',  { desc = 'Quit window' })
     vim.keymap.set('n', '<Esc>', '<cmd>nohlsearch<CR>', { desc = 'Clear search highlight' })
3. Add one mapping of your own that you'd actually use. Ideas:
     keep the cursor centered when paging:  vim.keymap.set('n', '<C-d>', '<C-d>zz')
     move selected lines down / up:         vim.keymap.set('x', 'J', ":m '>+1<CR>gv=gv")
                                            vim.keymap.set('x', 'K', ":m '<-2<CR>gv=gv")
   (Pick a key Neovim doesn't map already: Y, for example, is y$ by default.)
4. Restart nvim and try them. List your leader mappings with :nmap <leader>

Read more: :help vim.keymap.set(), :help <Leader>, :help map-<cmd>

w=$(q 'vim.fn.maparg("<leader>w", "n")'); echo "$w" | grep -qi 'w' && ok "<leader>w -> $w" || bad "no <leader>w mapping" "vim.keymap.set('n', '<leader>w', '<cmd>write<CR>')"
x=$(q 'vim.fn.maparg("<leader>q", "n")'); [ -n "$x" ] && ok "<leader>q -> $x" || bad "no <leader>q mapping"
e=$(q 'vim.fn.maparg("<Esc>", "n")'); echo "$e" | grep -qi 'noh' && ok "<Esc> clears search highlight" || bad "<Esc> doesn't run :nohlsearch" "vim.keymap.set('n', '<Esc>', '<cmd>nohlsearch<CR>')"
maps='table.concat(vim.iter({"n","x","s","o","i","c","t"}):map(function(md) return vim.iter(vim.api.nvim_get_keymap(md)):map(function(m) return md .. " " .. m.lhs .. " " .. (m.rhs or ("<fn>" .. (m.desc or ""))) end):totable() end):flatten():totable(), "\n")'
defaults=$(nvim --headless --clean -c "lua io.stdout:write(tostring($maps))" -c 'qa!' 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort -u)
n=$(LC_ALL=C comm -23 <(q "$maps" | LC_ALL=C sort -u) <(printf '%s\n' "$defaults") | grep -cvE '^n ( w| q|<Esc>) ')
if [ -z "$defaults" ]; then bad "couldn't list Neovim's default mappings" "check that nvim --clean starts"
else [ "${n:-0}" -ge 1 ] && ok "$n mapping(s) of your own" || bad "no mapping of your own yet" "step 3: map a key Neovim doesn't already map"; fi
finish

instructions:
Add the options and the autocmd most Neovim users end up with.

1. In init.lua add:
     vim.opt.relativenumber = true   -- keep number = true too: you get a hybrid
     vim.opt.scrolloff = 8
     vim.opt.undofile = true
     vim.opt.smartcase = true        -- with ignorecase: case-sensitive once you type a capital
     vim.opt.splitright = true
     vim.opt.splitbelow = true
2. Highlight on yank:
     local grp = vim.api.nvim_create_augroup('my_config', { clear = true })
     vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('TextYankPost', {
       group = grp,
       callback = function() vim.hl.on_yank() end,
     })
3. Optional: spell checking on every file (`set spell`) is noisy in code.
   If you want it, make it prose-only:
     vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('FileType', { group = grp,
       pattern = { 'markdown', 'gitcommit', 'text' },
       callback = function() vim.opt_local.spell = true end })
4. Restart. Run yip and watch the flash. Try 5j using the relative numbers.

Read more: :help 'scrolloff', :help 'smartcase', :help nvim_create_autocmd(), :help vim.hl.on_yank()

instructions:
Install lazy.nvim, add a statusline, and add telescope for fuzzy finding.

1. Bootstrap lazy.nvim at the top of init.lua, right after mapleader (copy from
   https://lazy.folke.io/installation, the "Single File" setup). It clones lazy.nvim into
   ~/.local/share/nvim/lazy/ on first start, then you call:
     require('lazy').setup({
       spec = {
         { 'vim-airline/vim-airline' },  -- a statusline: optional, lualine.nvim or any other works too
         { 'nvim-telescope/telescope.nvim', dependencies = { 'nvim-lua/plenary.nvim' } },
       },
     })
2. Telescope mappings:
     local tb = require('telescope.builtin')
     vim.keymap.set('n', '<leader>ff', tb.find_files, { desc = 'Find files' })
     vim.keymap.set('n', '<leader>fg', tb.live_grep,  { desc = 'Grep' })
     vim.keymap.set('n', '<leader>fb', tb.buffers,    { desc = 'Buffers' })
     vim.keymap.set('n', '<leader>fh', tb.help_tags,  { desc = 'Help' })
   (Put these after require('lazy').setup(...), or in the plugin spec's `config`/`keys`.)
3. Restart nvim. lazy installs everything. Then :Lazy shows the status.
4. If you used vim-plug before, delete its leftovers once lazy works:
     rm -rf ~/.config/nvim/plugged ~/.local/share/nvim/site/autoload/plug.vim
5. Use it: in a project, <leader>ff to find a file and <leader>fg to grep.
   Ctrl-v opens the result in a vertical split.
   live_grep needs ripgrep (rg): apt install ripgrep, or brew install ripgrep.

Read more: :help lazy.nvim.txt, :help telescope.nvim

instructions:
Turn this leftover Vimscript into Lua: every `set` line into vim.opt, and the two
nnoremap lines into vim.keymap.set. Aim for three :s commands, not 9 line edits.
  set foo      -> vim.opt.foo = true
  set foo=val  -> vim.opt.foo = val
  nnoremap L R -> vim.keymap.set('n', 'L', 'R')
Hint: \(\w\+\) captures a word, \(\S\+\) captures non-space, \1 \2 reuse them.

start.main.txt:
set number
set relativenumber
set scrolloff=8
set tabstop=4
set ignorecase
set smartcase
set undofile
nnoremap Y y$
nnoremap n nzz

target.main.txt:
vim.opt.number = true
vim.opt.relativenumber = true
vim.opt.scrolloff = 8
vim.opt.tabstop = 4
vim.opt.ignorecase = true
vim.opt.smartcase = true
vim.opt.undofile = true
vim.keymap.set('n', 'Y', 'y$')
vim.keymap.set('n', 'n', 'nzz')
